accuracy.reason: All eight cards preserve boundaries: reverse proxy versus backend work, L4 connection versus L7 request, count versus actual load, sampled health versus success, affinity versus durable state, draining versus migration, uncertain write versus retry safety, and distribution versus capacity. No unsupported safety guarantee.

evidence.quote: The backend performs the work; the balancer chooses where traffic goes.

mechanisms.reason: Routing units and TLS visibility lead to policy selection; health sampling delays removal; local state explains failover loss. Card 6 follows new-assignment cutoff, existing connections and accepted requests to a deadline. Card 7 coordinates stable-key record and purchase effect atomically across replicas.

evidence.quote: Choose the routing unit and required HTTP visibility before choosing a balancing policy.

coherence.reason: HTTP connection and database-transaction prerequisites support the ordered cards: request path, routing unit, selection, health, state, draining, retry safety and path-wide capacity. Inspected reverse-proxy bidirectional flow and drain diagrams correctly separate new assignments from A remaining work; shared renderer/CSS inspected earlier, no runtime check claimed.

evidence.quote: Count requests or connections to select traffic, then measure the work those counts hide.

decisions.reason: Cards 1/3/8 give conditional need and policy choices, measured load and backend capacity, saturated-database limits, surviving headroom and tested reachable alternate entry. Cards 4-7 add fail-open policy checks, shared-session costs, bounded drains and delayed retry budgets.

evidence.quote: Health-based routing reduces exposure to failure; it cannot guarantee every request succeeds.

clarity.reason: Definitions explain backend, layers, readiness, affinity, in-flight work, deduplication and headroom when introduced. The reused-connection, lost-response and local-cart examples expose practical limits without promising equal work or zero interruptions.

evidence.quote: Routing a user consistently and making their state available on another server are separate responsibilities.

outcomes.reason: Learner traces both proxy directions and backend work, selects L7 with decrypted HTTP visibility for paths, scopes L4 selection to reused connections, and permits one adequate server absent distribution/redundancy needs.

Learner contrasts turns, active connection counts and weighted shares with each limitation, conditionally considers uneven work and capacity using measurement, identifies shared database saturation and requires reachable entry failover plus survivor headroom or visible load rejection.

Learner distinguishes endpoint response from database-dependent readiness, explains coverage/interval/threshold delay and post-probe failure, limits removal to future selection, and denies repair, undo or safe replay of in-flight work; all-unhealthy behavior is checked.

Learner explains B lacks A memory and A failure can lose the only cart, weighs affinity placement/load costs without replication guarantees, and gives shared storage access/coordination/availability costs.

Learner stops new assignments, manages existing connection/request acceptance, allows and tracks accepted work until a bounded deadline, and permits forced interruption without migration. L4 reused connections and L7 accepted-work distinction are explicit.

Learner treats timeout as unknown committed outcome, reuses one logical key across all backends with shared durable result and atomic unique reservation/effect/result, rejects fresh keys and A-only memory, and bounds/delays retries to avoid overload.

sourceChecks.claim: Live AWS ELB introduction confirms traffic distribution across backend targets and redundant-serving purpose; lesson scopes its concrete path to a reverse proxy.
Live Azure overview supports L4 TCP/UDP versus L7 path routing and TLS offload; official NLB followup explicitly binds each TCP connection to one target for its lifetime.
Live NGINX documentation confirms round robin, least active connections and configured weighted request shares; lesson correctly treats these as signals with workload limits.
Live AWS health-check reference confirms periodic sampling, thresholds and all-unhealthy fail-open behavior; readiness and in-flight limitations follow the stated probe scope.
Live ASP.NET web-farm guidance supports independent node caches and shared distributed state; affinity routing cannot copy process memory or preserve a failed sole copy.

Live AWS deregistration guidance stops new request assignment and waits for in-flight completion within delay, with early termination errors. L4 connection-lifetime followup supports the explicit reused-connection drain warning.

Previously live-inspected AWS idempotent API article supports stable request identifiers and atomic durable token/effect recording; lesson adds bounded delayed attempts without claiming the proxy provides this guarantee.

Live Google SRE overload chapter requires accepting work only as capacity frees and gracefully rejecting excess, warns cascading failures and retry amplification. Available alternate entry and headroom are explicitly required, not inferred from box count.
